You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Alphabet Q2 2026 Earnings Highlights: Google Cloud Revenue Surges 82% Above Expectations, Backlog Hits $514 Billion, Free Cash Flow Turns Negative as Full-Year Capex Guidance Raised

TEXT:
Core View
Alphabet reported Q2 2026 results with total revenue of $119.796 billion, up 24% year-over-year. Operating income reached $40.77 billion, up 30% YoY, with operating margin expanding 2 percentage points to 34%. Net income attributable to common shareholders was $112.107 billion, up 298% YoY, primarily driven by approximately $97.98 billion in unrealized gains on equity securities (including holdings in Anthropic and SpaceX). The standout was Google Cloud, which delivered $24.768 billion in revenue, significantly beating the $22.42 billion consensus and surging 82% YoY—the fastest growth rate in recent years. Cloud operating income jumped to $8.814 billion from $2.826 billion a year earlier. Cloud backlog (contracted but unrecognized revenue) reached $514 billion, crossing the $500 billion mark for the first time and signaling that large-scale AI investments are converting into commercial returns. However, Q2 capital expenditures of $44.92 billion pushed free cash flow negative at –$5.855 billion.
The company raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195–205 billion. Shares fluctuated after the release, dropping more than 4% at one point amid investor concerns over the scale and return timeline of AI infrastructure spending.
Detailed Breakdown
Overall Revenue and Profit Performance
Total revenue: $119.796 billion, up 24% YoY (23% on a constant-currency basis), marking the 12th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.
Operating income: $40.77 billion, up 30% YoY; operating margin rose 2 percentage points to 34%.
Net income: $112.107 billion, up 298% YoY, largely driven by ~$97.98 billion in unrealized gains on equity securities.
Free cash flow: –$5.855 billion for the quarter (turned negative due to elevated capital spending); trailing twelve-month free cash flow remained solid at $53.273 billion.
Key drivers: AI-related demand strongly boosted the cloud business while the core advertising franchise remained resilient.
Google Cloud Performance
Revenue: $24.768 billion, beating the $22.42 billion expectation and rising 82% YoY (fastest growth in recent years).
Operating income: $8.814 billion, up sharply from $2.826 billion in the prior-year period, reflecting meaningful profitability improvement.
Backlog: $514 billion—the first time exceeding $500 billion—indicating that AI investments are translating into long-term contracted revenue.
Growth drivers: Strong demand for Google Cloud Platform (GCP) enterprise AI solutions, AI infrastructure, and core cloud services. Nearly 90% of Fortune 100 companies are now using Gemini Enterprise.
Other Business Segment Performance
Google Services total revenue: $94.54 billion, up 15% YoY.
Search & other: $63.271 billion, up 17% YoY (slightly below the $63.28 billion expectation).
YouTube ads: $11.055 billion, up 13% YoY.
Subscriptions, platforms, and devices: $12.911 billion, up 15% YoY.
Overall advertising business continued steady expansion, with AI features (such as AI Overviews) contributing incremental growth.
Capital Expenditure Plans
Q2 capital expenditures: $44.92 billion, above the $44.15 billion consensus and nearly double the $22.446 billion spent in the year-ago quarter; primarily allocated to data centers, AI servers, and computing infrastructure.
Full-year 2026 capex guidance: Raised to $195–205 billion (from the prior $180–190 billion range).
Financing support: Raised a net $49.6 billion in June through Class A, Class C, and mandatory convertible preferred shares; issued $2.03 billion in senior unsecured notes; established an at-the-market equity program of up to $40 billion (not yet initiated as of quarter-end).
Primary investment focus: Expanding AI infrastructure and data-center capacity to meet surging cloud demand.
Next-Quarter and Full-Year Guidance-Related Information
The company did not provide specific numerical guidance for Q3 2026 revenue or operating income.
The key update was the upward revision of full-year capital expenditures to $195–205 billion to support accelerating AI and cloud demand.
Additional operating metrics: Gemini App monthly active users reached 950 million (above the prior estimate of 920 million); Gemini models are processing 22 billion API tokens per minute.
Market Context and Investor Concerns
Core tension: Cloud and AI commercialization results were strong (revenue beat, record backlog, and improved profitability), yet the scale of capital spending caused free cash flow to turn negative in the quarter, raising questions about the return timeline on AI infrastructure investments.
Stock reaction: Shares fluctuated post-earnings and declined more than 4% at one point.
CEO Sundar Pichai stated: “Our AI investments are redefining the possibilities in every part of our business,” highlighting a differentiated full-stack AI strategy that is delivering measurable value to consumers, enterprise customers, and partners.
Overall assessment: AI spending is shifting from pure investment phase toward earnings realization, with Google Cloud established as the primary growth engine; elevated capital expenditures remain the main near-term focus for the market.
